q: What is the usual safe order for simplifying a CFG?
options: Remove ε-productions, then unit productions, then useless symbols
Remove useless symbols, then unit productions, then ε-productions
Remove unit productions, then ε-productions, then useless symbols
explain: Removing ε can create unit productions, and both steps can make symbols useless. So useless symbols are removed last.

options: A never appears on the right side of a production
explain: Nullable variables can derive the empty string. They are found by a fixpoint: A → ε, or A → B₁…Bₖ with every Bᵢ nullable.

q: A symbol is useless when it is…
options: used in more than one production
explain: A useful symbol must derive some terminal string (generating) and appear in some derivation from S (reachable). Failing either one makes it useless.

q: When removing useless symbols, which should be removed first?
explain: Removing non-generating variables can cut off other symbols, making them unreachable. Doing reachability first can leave useless symbols behind.

q: Simplify S → AB | a, A → a, B → bB. What remains?
options: S → AB, A → a, B → b
explain: B is non-generating (it never terminates), so S → AB goes. Then A is unreachable from S. Only S → a is left.

q: Which of these is a unit production?
explain: A unit production has exactly one variable on the right side. A → a is a terminal rule, and A → BC is a binary rule.

q: Removing ε-productions from S → aSb | ε (ignoring whether ε itself stays in the language) gives…
explain: S is nullable, so S → aSb gets a copy without S, which is S → ab. The result generates aⁿbⁿ for n ≥ 1. A new start rule is added if ε must be kept.

q: In S → AB, A → aA | ε, B → bB | ε, which variables are nullable?
explain: A → ε and B → ε make A and B nullable. Then S → AB has both symbols nullable, so S is nullable too.

q: Simplifying a CFG never changes the language it generates, apart from possibly having to treat ε separately.
explain: True. Every step is designed to keep exactly the same set of terminal strings. Only ε may need a special start rule after the ε-productions are removed.

q: In S → aA | B, A → a, B → bB, which variable is non-generating?
explain: Every B-production contains B again, so B never yields a terminal string. S still generates 'aa' through A.
